# Canon Mirrorless System — Travel, Family, Portrait, Landscape, Macro

A citation-backed buying guide for a **photography beginner** choosing a Canon
mirrorless (RF) system that is **lightweight** and must handle **travel now**,
then **family and macro later** — plus **arthritis-friendly accessories** and
**lightweight thumb-lock tripods**. Canon-only scope.

New to camera terms? Open the **[glossary](glossary.md)** first. Full reasoning
is in **[canon-mirrorless-system.md](canon-mirrorless-system.md)**; every claim
is sourced in **[citations.md](citations.md)** (84 sources). Independent
verification is in **[audit/](audit/)**.

## What it answers

Whether one Canon system can do all five jobs (yes), which **single lens
combines portrait + landscape** (a 24–105 zoom), what "lightweight" really costs
you, and which tripods/accessories suit limited hand strength.

## The recommendation (lightest capable starting kit)

| Piece | Pick | Why |
|-------|------|-----|
| Body | **EOS R50** (APS-C, 375 g) [[1]](citations.md#c1) | Lightest/cheapest capable beginner body |
| One-lens travel | **RF-S 18-150mm** (~305 g) [[46]](citations.md#c46) | Wide → portrait reach in one light lens |
| Portrait add-on | **RF 50mm f/1.8 STM** (160 g, ~$200) [[20]](citations.md#c20) | Cheap, light, blurred backgrounds |
| Macro (later) | **RF 85mm f/2 Macro** (~499 g) [[36]](citations.md#c36) | Portrait + 0.5× close-up in one |
| Tripod | **Peak Design Travel** or **Manfrotto Befree lever** [[78]](citations.md#c78)[[81]](citations.md#c81) | Flip/lever leg locks — thumb-friendly |
| Arthritis aids | **BR-E1 remote + touchscreen + hand strap + lever QR clamp** [[74]](citations.md#c74)[[67]](citations.md#c67)[[68]](citations.md#c68)[[69]](citations.md#c69) | Removes grip-and-press strain |

**Step up** to full-frame **EOS R8** (461 g, still light) [[2]](citations.md#c2)
or IBIS-equipped **R6 II** [[3]](citations.md#c3) if family low-light and
in-body stabilization outrank cost.

## Total kit weight (lightweight is the priority)

| Kit | Weight |
|-----|--------|
| R100 + RF-S 18-45mm | ~486 g [[6]](citations.md#c6)[[47]](citations.md#c47) |
| **R50 + RF-S 18-150mm (recommended)** | **~680 g** [[1]](citations.md#c1)[[46]](citations.md#c46) |
| R8 + RF 24-105mm f/4-7.1 | ~856 g [[2]](citations.md#c2)[[43]](citations.md#c43) |
| R6 II + RF 24-105mm f/4L | ~1,380 g [[3]](citations.md#c3)[[42]](citations.md#c42) |

The **lens drives weight more than the body** [[63]](citations.md#c63) — choose
the lens for weight first.

## Quick decision framework

1. **Budget + lightest, one lens?** → R50 + RF-S 18-150mm (~680 g, ~$1,100 kit).
2. **Want better low-light family photos / stabilization?** → R8 (light
   full-frame) or R6 II (has IBIS) [[2]](citations.md#c2)[[3]](citations.md#c3).
3. **Macro a near-term serious goal?** → R7 (APS-C, IBIS, +reach) + RF 100mm
   f/2.8L (true 1:1) [[4]](citations.md#c4)[[36]](citations.md#c36).
4. **Buying APS-C?** → you also unlock cheaper/lighter **Sigma/Tamron** lenses
   (RF third-party is **APS-C only**) [[53]](citations.md#c53)[[55]](citations.md#c55).
5. **Tripod?** → insist on **flip/lever leg locks** + a **lever QR clamp**
   [[78]](citations.md#c78)[[69]](citations.md#c69).

## Three things to know before you buy

- **0.5× "Macro" is not true macro.** Only the RF 100mm f/2.8L reaches 1:1+
  (1.4×); the f/1.8 "Macro" primes are 0.5×
  [[36]](citations.md#c36)[[37]](citations.md#c37).
- **Third-party RF lenses are APS-C only** as of June 2026 — full-frame buyers
  use Canon glass only [[55]](citations.md#c55)[[62]](citations.md#c62).
- **Cheap bodies have no stabilization** (no IBIS, and cheap primes lack lens
  IS) — matters for handheld low-light and macro [[4]](citations.md#c4).
